title: Dip buys
oneLiner: Buys your agent's coin when it dips, a small fixed amount at a time, with SOL it can spare above a reserve.
howItWorks: Holds one limit buy of the coin at a time: buy_sol of it, once the on-chain price falls drop_pct under the price when the buy was set.
Highwire's order runner fills it, checking the whole policy, simulating and logging it like any trade.
After a fill it waits cooldown_hours, then sets the next buy under the price then, so a falling price is bought step by step.
If the price instead rises reset_rise_pct over where the buy was set, it cancels the buy and sets a new one under the new price.
It sets a buy only while the wallet would still hold keep_sol after it.

notes.drop_pct: How far under the price when it's set a buy fills, in percent.
notes.keep_sol: SOL the wallet always keeps: no buy is set that would spend into it.
notes.cooldown_hours: How long after a fill (or a failed one) the next buy is set.
notes.reset_rise_pct: How far the price must rise over where the buy was set before the buy moves up.
notes.expires_days: Each buy expires after this many days; the next wake-up sets a fresh one.
notes.slippage_bps: The most slippage a fill may take, in basis points (500 is 5%).

wire: On every wake-up of the loop, once the coin's mint is known, call tendDips(mint) inside a try/catch, and log the line it returns (once, not on every wake-up when it hasn't changed).
Nothing else: the order runner that `npm start` already runs fills the buy.
prompt: Read modules/dip-buys.md, then wire the dip-buys module into src/agent.ts as its "Wiring it in" section says. Don't change dips.json or the policy; tell me what the policy needs.
risks: A dip can keep falling: each buy can lose value like any trade.
The policy's daily cap covers dip buys and every other spend together, so a busy day can crowd one out.
A fill can take days, or never come if the price only rises. That's the module working, not failing.
